attacks.claim: The staging QA that reports 0 failures and 11 min for 50k recipients was run with SES throttling simulated off, after 4 workers were throttled at the 14 msg/s staging cap. Production has never been tested against real SES throttling, so the throughput and failure-handling results do not transfer to production.
attacks.evidence: "4 workers were throttled intermittently, so QA ran with SES throttling simulated off via the sandbox mock"

attacks.claim: Production config runs 48 workers at ~25 msg/s each, roughly 1,200 msg/s, about 4x the 300 msg/s SES account limit. Sustained over-quota sending will produce throttling, and the worker records throttling as permanent per-recipient failures.
attacks.evidence: "SEND_WORKERS=48" / "BATCH_SIZE=50" / "Per-worker throughput | 1 worker, batch 50 | ~25 msg/s sustained" / "SES production account limits (us-east-1): 300 messages/second"

attacks.claim: On any batch-level SES error, including transient throttling, every recipient in the batch is recorded in send_failures and excluded from the rest of the issue, with no retry. Subscribers who were never attempted are reported to publishers as 'Not delivered', and a throttling burst can silently drop large parts of an issue.
attacks.evidence: "for _, r := range batch.Recipients { failures.Record(ctx, batch.IssueID, r.SubscriberID, errCode(err)) }" / "those recipients are excluded from the issue's remaining sends"

attacks.claim: Per-recipient status is matched by position (batch.Recipients[i]) with no length or key check. A short or reordered SES response misattributes failures to the wrong subscribers, corrupting exclusion and the 'Not delivered' report.
attacks.evidence: "for i, res := range out.BulkEmailEntryResults { ... batch.Recipients[i].SubscriberID ... }"

attacks.claim: The error path skips q.Ack and does not retry or document redelivery, so batch ownership after failure is undefined. This risks duplicate sends or silent loss depending on queue semantics. A timeout after SES accepted the call would also mark delivered recipients as failed.
attacks.evidence: "metrics.Inc(\"send.batch_failed\") continue ... q.Ack(ctx, batch) (only reached on success path)"

attacks.claim: The SES call has no stated timeout, retry policy, or retryable-vs-terminal error classification, so a hung SendBulkEmail can block a worker indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: per-call timeout, retry policy, or retryable vs terminal error classification

attacks.claim: Smart Send Time is on by default for all publications and can hold issues up to 18 hours. Time-sensitive news content (breaking news, election results, weather alerts) would be delayed for subscribers, and about 40% of publications are in that cohort, with no exemption or bypass.
attacks.evidence: "Enabled by default for all publications; publishers can turn it off in Settings → Delivery" / "SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=on" / "4,480 of them (40%) are news or local-news outlets whose issues are time-sensitive (breaking news, election results, weather alerts)"

attacks.claim: Prod config sets SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=on at deploy, contradicting the stated 5%→25%→100% cohort ramp, so the full default-on exposure happens on day one.
attacks.evidence: "SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=on" / "ramp SMART_SEND_DEFAULT by publication cohort: 5% (week 1), 25% (week 2), 100% (week 3)"

attacks.claim: The public launch post goes to all publishers at 16:00 UTC claiming Smart Send is live for everyone and that issues arrive up to 5x faster. Neither claim is validated at production scale, and the post contradicts the staged rollout. A sent announcement cannot be recalled.
attacks.evidence: "every Inkwell issue reaches inboxes up to 5× faster" / "Smart Send Time is live for every publication today" / "Nothing to set up; it's already on."

attacks.claim: The 5x speed claim is unsupported: the goal is 14 min to under 3 min (about 4.7x), and the only measured run is 11 min in staging with throttling off.
attacks.evidence: "Goal: cut median time-to-inbox for a 50k-subscriber issue from 14 min to under 3 min" / "11 min"

attacks.claim: Smart Send's prediction accuracy is 71% within ±1h, a prediction metric rather than a delivery guarantee. It has no quality gate before default-on, and the rollout gate (open-rate lift ≥3%) does not measure harm to time-sensitive content.
attacks.evidence: "predicted hour within ±1h of actual top open hour, 2,000 sampled subscribers | — | 71%"

attacks.claim: Rollback is underspecified. Pipeline rollback does not reconcile recipients already written to send_failures, which stay excluded after switching back to Sidekiq, and dual-sender drain has no duplicate-send guard. Smart Send rollback says held issues are 'released immediately' without saying whether they go out at once or per-subscriber schedule.
attacks.evidence: "Rollback (pipeline): set SENDER=sidekiq in the dispatcher; in-flight batches drain in < 2 min." / "Rollback (Smart Send): set SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=off; held issues are released immediately."

attacks.claim: Smart Send builds a per-subscriber model from 90 days of open behavior. The artifact gives no subscriber-facing notice, consent basis, or per-recipient opt-out, only a publisher-level toggle, which is a compliance exposure under GDPR/ePrivacy-style rules.
attacks.evidence: "predicts each subscriber's most likely open hour from their last 90 days of opens" / "publishers can turn it off in Settings → Delivery" / "ABSENT: legal review or subscriber-facing disclosure of open-hour prediction"

attacks.claim: Alerting does not cover the likely failure modes. The pager fires on queue lag and complaints only, with no alarm on send.batch_failed, send_failures growth, Not-delivered counts, or SES throttling/quota errors. The complaint alarm thresholds (0.08% vs 0.1%) are also inconsistent.
attacks.evidence: "On-call pager: queue lag > 10 min, complaint rate > 0.1%" / "SES bounce/complaint rate (alarms at 4% / 0.08%)"

attacks.claim: Pipeline cutover is 100% of sends on Monday with no canary or percentage ramp, while Smart Send does get a cohort ramp. The 48-worker scale was never exercised in staging.
attacks.evidence: "deploy Monday 09:00 UTC to 100% of sends"

attacks.claim: Scale of Smart Send is unsized: no numbers for prediction compute, hold-queue storage, or per-hour batching at 10-100x subscriber counts. The 50k QA run is the only data point.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: hold-queue sizing, prediction compute cost, behaviour at 10-100x subscribers

attacks.claim: The public launch is on the same day as deploy, seven hours later, leaving no soak window at production volume before the irreversible announcement.
attacks.evidence: "Deploy: Mon 2026-11-09 09:00 UTC · Launch post: Mon 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC"

attacks.claim: Suppression and bounce handling across the new bulk path are not described, and deliverability reputation protection under over-quota sending is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: "SES_CONFIGURATION_SET=inkwell-prod" / "Bounce/complaint webhooks still processed | — | Pass"

attacks.claim: Sending depends on a single provider in us-east-1 with no documented fallback or data-residency statement for subscriber data.
attacks.evidence: "SES_REGION=us-east-1"

attacks.claim: No spend ceiling or projected daily volume is given, so retry-storm or runaway-send cost exposure cannot be estimated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: projected daily message volume and spend ceiling
